title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar at the First Round Table Conference: Speaking for the Depressed Classes (1930)
summary: In November 1930, inside St. James's Palace in London, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar delivered a historic maiden speech asserting that India's marginalized millions demanded complete political sovereignty and equal citizenship.
full_text:
In November 1930, inside the gilded halls of St. James's Palace in London, King George V inaugurated the First Indian Round Table Conference to deliberate upon constitutional reform for the subcontinent.

The assembly was filled with imperial viceroys, maharajas draped in pearls, and elite Indian politicians. Rising from the benches, thirty-nine-year-old Dr. B. R. Ambedkar addressed the gathering on behalf of India's fifty million marginalized untouchables.

His words rang out with devastating moral force:
"My Lords and Gentlemen, we have heard extensive praises sung of the benefits of the British Empire. But I speak on behalf of the Depressed Classes of India—a fifth of the entire population—who have been treated as outcasts and denied the basic rights of human beings. What has British rule achieved for us?

In one hundred and fifty years, has the British Government removed our social degradation? No! Our children are still excluded from common schools, our mothers are forbidden from village wells, and our people are consigned to social servitude. The bureaucratic government has maintained a policy of callous neutrality toward social oppression!
We refuse to be treated as pawns in imperial diplomacy. We demand self-government, but we demand a democratic constitution in which our political representation is guaranteed, our human rights are protected, and our people stand as equal citizens endowed with sovereign power. We will accept nothing less!"

Ambedkar’s courage and formidable constitutional precision captured the attention of international statesmen, permanently establishing the Depressed Classes as an autonomous political force in modern history.
